Jamal: Quick heads-up — noticed authz routing misattribution for SA tokens in prod for two customers. When the exchange goes through the edge proxy the quota/usage shows up under the router service instead of the customer org/project. Anyone seen this?
Maria: Yup — saw weird quota spikes on the router nodes around 02:10 UTC. Thought it was a routing loop at first. :facepalm:
Sophie: Could be the claim rewrite we added in the auth-proxy. We normalize claims to reduce header size. Do we drop origin org/project there?
Raoul: We don't drop them, but we do rewrite `x-effective-identity` to the proxy's principal during exchange. That header is the source for the billing attribution pipeline right now.
Linh: Minimal repro: client -> edge-proxy (exchange) -> router -> inference. After exchange the `x-origin-org` header is missing and `x-effective-identity` is `service/router@redwood`.
Jamal: OK that explains it. The attribution pipeline prefers `x-effective-identity` over `x-origin-org` for backward compatibility. Need to decide priority.
Maria: Short-term mitigation: can we fallback to `x-origin-org` if `x-effective-identity` looks like a router principal? i.e. `if principal.endswith("@redwood") then prefer origin`.
Sophie: That seems reasonable. But watch out for legitimate internal tenants. We need a robust check: maybe a mapping of known infra principals vs customer principals.
Raoul: Mapping exists but it's large and not always up-to-date. Alternative: pass through an `x-origin-signed` claim from auth service during exchange to prove provenance — then attribution can trust it.
Linh: That would require a tiny protocol change on exchange: auth-service returns `origin_claim_sig` and proxy forwards it. Minimal patch: auth exchange response adds `origin_sig`.
Jamal: Sounds good for long term. Short term: can we flip a telemetry flag to mark suspected events so billing doesn't ingest them? I want to avoid retroactive credits.
Maria: We can add a filtering rule in the attribution ETL: if `x-effective-identity` in infra-principal-list AND `x-origin-org` present -> prefer `x-origin-org`. Roll it for 24h to see impact.
Sophie: Also increase sampling for these flows to 100% for the next 6 hours so we have traces. Add a dashboard tile showing counts where attribution differs (effective vs origin).
Raoul: I'll open an infra ticket for the long-term `origin_sig` plan and link the PR.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollback triggered for auth-proxy v2.3.1 -> rolling back to v2.3.0 due to unrelated health check flaps (FYI).
Linh: Note: if we rollback the proxy we might lose the new header behavior — we'll still need the ETL rule to be safe.
Jamal: Action items: 1) Sophie -> add ETL fallback rule + dashboard tile (short term) 2) Raoul -> infra ticket for `origin_sig` and design doc 3) Maria/Linh -> run 100% sampling on affected paths for 6h and paste traces in ticket.
Maria: I'll schedule a quick 15m sync in 30m to confirm rollout steps.
Sophie: Putting the dashboard patch on my queue now. Will ping when ready for review.
Raoul: Opening ticket: INFRA-4129 "origin-sig: signed provenance for auth exchange" and linking this thread.
Jamal: Thanks — let's avoid billing surprises. 
Maria: :thumbsup:
